ncai.externalMcp.description: Expose OpsBatch as an MCP server for external clients such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Grok. Uses the same catalog tools as in-app agents (terminal, SFTP, Vault, port forwarding). Keep OpsBatch running while clients are connected.
ncai.externalMcp.enableForLauncher: Enable External MCP to get a usable launcher path.
ncai.externalMcp.focusOnHostOpen.descrip: When an MCP client opens a host, bring the main window to the foreground. Turn off to keep working without interruption.

ncai.externalMcp.http.allowCustomBind.de: By default the endpoint binds to 127.0.0.1. Turn this on for WSL2 NAT and set 0.0.0.0 or the vEthernet IP.
ncai.externalMcp.http.clientHost.descrip: Used in copied configs when the listener is 0.0.0.0 or ::. Enter the IP clients can reach, such as the Windows host IP.
ncai.externalMcp.http.clientHostRequired: Enter the IP clients should connect to. 0.0.0.0 is not a reachable address.
ncai.externalMcp.http.description: Serve the same External MCP tools over Streamable HTTP for clients that cannot launch the stdio CLI, such as Codex inside WSL. Off by default.
ncai.externalMcp.http.invalidAddress: Listen address must be an IP, such as 0.0.0.0 or the vEthernet IP.
ncai.externalMcp.http.invalidClientHost: Client address must be a reachable IP, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
ncai.externalMcp.http.legacySseNote: Legacy HTTP+SSE (2024-11-05) is not offered. Use this Streamable HTTP URL.
ncai.externalMcp.http.portHint: Fixed port, default 47391. Client URLs stay the same across restarts. Allowed range: 1024–65535.
ncai.externalMcp.http.regenerateHint: Issues a new bearer token. HTTP clients must use the new token. The stdio discovery file is updated; clients that are already connected over stdio stay connected.
ncai.externalMcp.http.requiresExternalMc: Turn on External MCP before this endpoint will listen.
ncai.externalMcp.http.title: Streamable HTTP
ncai.externalMcp.http.warning: Listening beyond 127.0.0.1 exposes External MCP to other machines that can reach this address. Keep the bearer token private and do not publish this port.
ncai.externalMcp.http.wslHint: With WSL mirrored networking, localhost works. Otherwise listen on 0.0.0.0 or the vEthernet IP and set Client address to the Windows host IP.
ncai.externalMcp.idleTimeout.description: In temporary mode, disable External MCP after this many minutes with no MCP operations.

ncai.externalMcp.mode.description: Temporary mode auto-disables after idle timeout. Always-on restores External MCP when OpsBatch starts.

ncai.externalMcp.permissionMode.hint: Same setting as Settings → AI → Safety. Auto runs OpsBatch write tools without OpsBatch approval prompts; Confirm asks each time. External clients (Codex / Claude / Grok) may still show their own tool approval UI.
ncai.externalMcp.permissionMode.label: Write permission mode
ncai.externalMcp.security.description: Listens on 127.0.0.1 with a rotating token, reuses AI Permission Mode for writes, and removes discovery when disabled. No OAuth — this is a local desktop bridge.
ncai.externalMcp.sessionIdleTimeout.desc: Automatically close sessions opened by an AI after this many minutes without terminal or file activity.
ncai.externalMcp.silentSessions.descript: Sessions opened by AI stay out of your tab bar and are not restored after restart. View them anytime from the tray panel.
ncai.externalMcp.title: External MCP
ncai.externalMcp.usage.capabilities: 4. Full catalog tools are available: terminal, SFTP, Vault, and port forwarding. Secrets (passwords / private keys) are never returned.
ncai.externalMcp.usage.keepRunning: 1. Turn on External MCP and keep OpsBatch running.
ncai.externalMcp.usage.localhost: 2. Clients connect via the local launcher (127.0.0.1 only). Discovery is removed when you disable the switch.
ncai.externalMcp.usage.permissions: 3. Write operations follow Settings → AI → Safety (observer / confirm / auto) and the command blocklist.
ncai.externalMcp.usage.title: How to use
